How a founder made $1,000 from an app everyone said was useless.

//Read this if you doubt yourself...(Short story great lesson) 

He built a subscription-tracking app in one of the most saturated markets ever.
Everyone told him it would flop because:

• Rocket Money exists
• There are endless free alternatives
• The market is “dead”

But he built it anyway.

His first move? Mass-DMing 100–200 strangers complaining about subscription charges.
98% ghosted him. 0 conversions.
Painful. Character-building. Ego-destroying.
But he didn’t quit.

On September 22nd, he launched publicly on Reddit, HackerNews, and ProductHunt.
Within a few hours: 2 paying users.
Not huge, but enough to spark the “oh damn, this might actually work” moment.

He began documenting everything, revenue, learning, progress, failures.
By the end of October:
$157 revenue | 20 paid users.

Then November hit… and his posts started going viral.

With virality came the haters:
• “AI slop”
• “A subscription to track subscriptions?”
• “Just use the free alternative”

He kept going anyway.

People also told him he was underpricing, so he tested raising his price from $7.50 → $22.50.
Conversion rate? Didn’t even drop.
Testimonials? Started rolling in.
Momentum? Activated.

Results:
• November revenue: $768
• Total revenue: $1000+
• Paid users: 90+
• December already at $100+

Two months ago, he thought nobody wanted his app.
Today, people are literally pulling out cards to pay him.

✨ Lessons:
Your product isn’t usually the problem. Your distribution is.
Build in public.
Tell your story.
Price your value. 
Keep going even when it feels cringe.
If you want to make money from yours SaaS, do these and Focus on marketing as well.

//Story is from Reddit
